subject: Microbiology
subtopic: EBV biology, B-cell tropism, infectious mononucleosis, complications and diagnosis
concept: Epstein-Barr virus (human herpesvirus 4) is a ubiquitous herpesvirus with B-cell tropism that establishes lifelong latency.

content.definition: Primary EBV infection can cause infectious mononucleosis with fever, pharyngitis, lymphadenopathy and atypical lymphocytosis.
content.explanation: EBV infects epithelial cells and B lymphocytes, then establishes lifelong latency in B cells.
content.mechanism: The host immune response to infected B cells produces many clinical and hematologic features of infectious mononucleosis.
content.structure: EBV is an enveloped DNA herpesvirus.
content.function: Viral tropism for B cells and latency determine persistent infection and disease patterns.
causes: Saliva is the major transmission route
Blood and transplanted tissues can transmit EBV in specific settings
effects: Neurologic or severe disease can occur especially in immunocompromised patients
content.diagnosis: Heterophile antibody testing or EBV-specific serology is used according to age and clinical context; CBC findings support but do not alone establish infection.
content.treatment: Management of uncomplicated infectious mononucleosis is mainly supportive; severe or complicated disease requires specialist management.
high_yield: Fever, pharyngitis and lymphadenopathy are classic

terminology.etymology: Mono refers to mononuclear/monocytic blood-cell appearance.
terminology.notes: Common clinical syndrome of primary EBV infection.

terminology.etymology: Atypical means differing from the usual form.
terminology.notes: Reactive lymphocyte commonly seen in infectious mononucleosis.

yemen_context.relevance: Relevant to hematology and infectious-disease education; no unsupported Yemen-specific incidence is asserted.

review_notes: Original synthesis based on CDC clinical overview.
